name: Calendarized Butterfly (Time Butterfly)
summary: Sell two near-term ATM options and buy one longer-dated option at a lower strike and one at a higher strike; a butterfly whose wings live in a later expiry, so it holds value longer than a standard fly.

legs.strike_rule: Lower wing: strike below the body by 1 x the front-month expected move, or by delta 0.70-0.80.
Upper wing: strike above the body by the same distance as the lower wing (symmetric width), delta 0.20-0.30.
legs.dte_rule: back expiry, same as the lower wing

max_profit: Near the body strike at front expiry; larger than a same-expiry butterfly because the back-month wings retain time value. No closed form - model both wings at front expiry with back-month IV.
max_loss: Net debit plus, on the upper side, the unmatched (upper wing strike - body strike) x 100 exposure that exists only in the window between the two expiries if the position is mishandled. Managed correctly and closed before front expiry, the loss is the net debit.
breakevens: Two, inside the wings, solved numerically at front expiry with back-month IV.

greeks.gamma: negative and concentrated at the body
greeks.theta: positive, larger than a standard butterfly because the wings decay slower
greeks.vega: positive (the two long wings are back-month); a standard butterfly is near vega-flat, this one is not

when_to_use: IV rank < 30 with a strong pin thesis and a desire for a wider, longer-lived tent than a same-expiry butterfly. The back-month wings mean the structure does not go to zero value if the underlying moves - it degrades gracefully. Rarely worth the complexity outside SPY/QQQ.
entry_rules: IV rank < 30; front_IV - back_IV >= -2.0 vol points.
Body ATM by delta 0.45-0.55; wings symmetric in strike distance, sized at 1.0 x the front-month expected move.
Front body 21-35 DTE; wings 45-70 DTE; gap 21-35 days.
Net debit <= 2% of equity per unit; 4-leg bid-ask <= 10% of debit.
No earnings or ex-dividend in the front cycle.

LEVEL 3 OK but with a caveat the automation must encode: the lower-strike back-month long fully covers one short body contract (long strike < short strike, later expiry). The SECOND short body contract is covered by the UPPER wing only by strike, so Alpaca will hold (upper wing strike - body strike) x 100 minus the credit on that pair as maintenance. Verify the reserved buying power before sizing.
Submit as a single 4-leg mleg; if legging, buy BOTH wings first, then sell the body.
management_rules: If |spot - body strike| > 0.8 x the wing width, close the structure - the fly has lost its geometry.
If |net delta| > 0.30 per unit, close rather than adjust.
Roll the body out one expiry at front DTE <= 7 only if both shorts' |delta| <= 0.60, for a credit.
exit_rules: Close or roll BOTH short body contracts by 14:30 ET on front expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the whole structure no later than 2 trading days before the body's expiry if not rolling.
Close a short body contract immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05 or |delta| >= 0.90.
Close short calls before ex-dividend if extrinsic < dividend per share.
Unwind the body (shorts) before the wings (longs), always - the wings are the cover.
If either wing marks below $0.10, close everything.
assignment_risk: Two short body contracts. If both are assigned the account is short 200 shares against two long back-month calls at different strikes - covered, but with a directional gap between the wing strikes. Flatten within one session.
buying_power: Net debit plus a maintenance requirement of (upper wing strike - body strike) x 100 minus the credit on the pair whose cover is the upper wing. Do not assume debit-only.
liquidity_needs: Four legs across two expiries and three strikes: OI >= 500 per leg, penny-wide preferred. SPY/QQQ/IWM and mega-caps only.
common_mistakes: Assuming the buying-power requirement is just the debit; setting wings too narrow so the structure is all gamma and no tent; failing to recognize that the body is a DOUBLE short and therefore a double assignment candidate at front expiry.
zero_dte_notes: Not suitable - two 0DTE shorts on a share-settled name is exactly what the assignment policy forbids.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
